verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Friday, April 10, 2026'; R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT ... April 10'; R2: 'April 10, 2026' implied in updates; all confirm splashdown on April 10, 2026.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm return via splashdown on April 10, 2026; R3 explicitly states 'Friday'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; identical in R3, R4, R5.
verifications.reasoning: Exact match across all references for location, time, and time zones.

verifications.claim: The splashdown concluded a 10-day journey around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R3: 'ending historic 10-day mission to the moon'; R4: 'record-breaking 10-day mission'; R5: '10-day trip to the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as a 10-day journey around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew had recovery by the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fly them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; R2: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; identical confirmation in R3, R4, R5.
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly state recovery by USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: The capsule hit the upper atmosphere at roughly 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m.: ... first contact with the upper atmosphere'; R2: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere'; R3, R5 match exactly.
verifications.reasoning: Precise time and description of upper atmosphere entry match across sources.

verifications.claim: Drogue parachutes deployed around 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:03 p.m.: ... the drogue parachutes will deploy'; R2: '8:03 p.m. ... the drogue parachutes on Orion deployed'; R3, R5 identical.
verifications.reasoning: Exact time for drogue parachute deployment confirmed.

verifications.claim: Main parachutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:04 p.m.: ... the three main parachutes will deploy'; R2: '8:04 p.m. ... three main parachutes deployed'; R3, R5 match.
verifications.reasoning: Exact time for main parachute deployment directly supported.

verifications.claim: Splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN!'; exact time confirmed in all sources.
verifications.reasoning: Precise splashdown time and date universally confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts were extracted and transferred via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha by 9:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: '9:34 p.m. ... safely extracted ... 9:56 p.m. ... flown to the USS John P. Murtha ... 9:58 p.m. ... safely aboard'; R4: '9:52 PM EDT ... hoisted ... 10:01 PM EDT ... onboard'; R5: '9:06 p.m. ... extraction ... 9:35 p.m. ... arrives'; R3: '9:37 pm ... left Orion'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources show extraction ~9:30-9:37 p.m. and arrival aboard after 9:58 p.m., contradicting 'by 9:07 p.m.' for both extraction and transfer.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded after 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R3: 'historic 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10-day flight'; consistent description despite precise duration ~9 days 1 hour.
verifications.reasoning: Mission universally referred to as 10-day despite exact elapsed time; direct support.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission tested the Orion spacecraft with a crew on board for the first time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'evaluated Orion’s systems in the deep-space environment ... astronauts directly operated'; R5: 'first crew to fly on NASA’s Orion spacecraft'; R2 implies first crewed return.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II as first crewed Orion mission testing systems with astronauts.
